title: Marine EOD Diver (MGySgt to Sgt) NMOS (2336), DC I&L
raw_text:
4.     MOS 2339, Marine EOD Diver (MGySgt to Sgt) NMOS (2336), DC I&L

    a. Summary. A Marine EOD Technician who is trained to dive and use
littoral explosive ordnance neutralization (LEON) equipment in the underwater
environment. This title and MOS will also be used to identify Marine
explosive ordnance disposal (EOD) diver billets in the T/Os.

    b. Prerequisites. Must be a graduate of the Naval School Explosive
Ordnance Disposal (NAVSCOLEOD) Course (N56GPX1).

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the Navy Scuba Diver Course (N2003E1) or the Navy Basic
Scuba Diver Course (A-433-0123) at the Naval Dive and Salvage Training
Center, Panama City, FL.

        (2) Complete the MK 16 Underwater Breathing Apparatus (UBA) Diver
Course (N204C11) at the Naval Dive and Salvage Training Center, Panama City,
FL.


                                              3-153                      Enclosure (1)
 3121                                                           NAVMC 1200.1L



        (3) Complete the EOD Basic Navy Underwater Course (N20B0Q1) at
NAVSCOLEOD, Eglin AFB Florida or must complete the LEON MOJT program
supervised by a Marine EOD Diver (MOS 2339).

        (4) Must maintain physically qualified per naval special warfare/
special operations physical to perform diver duties in accordance with inter-
service requirements established in NAVMED P-117 and reference, standards of
medical fitness.

    d. Duties. MGySgt to Sgt: Plans and Employs Marine EOD LEON equipment
to conduct underwater operations to detect, locate, reacquire, render safe/
neutralize, recover, exploit, and dispose of underwater explosive ordnance in
the very shallow water and surf zone.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Commercial Diver 49-9092.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.




                                         3-154                   Enclosure (1)
 3122                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
